text: Working with APIs is an important skill for modern developers. An API allows two programs to communicate, usually through HTTP requests such as GET or POST. When you send a request, the server often returns data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Most APIs require authentication, so you need an API key or token to prove who you are. Be careful with rate limits, because sending too many requests can get you blocked. Finally, always add error handling to your code. Servers can fail or return unexpected responses, so check status codes and handle problems gracefully.
